title: ProjectE 2-D field solver report
description: Output of tools/scripts/field_solver.py. Unlike the ipc-calc-report envelope this tool DOES have a verdict, because it can be given a --target and can also refuse to answer when its own grid error is too large. The distinguishing field against zdiff-solve-report/v1 is closed_form_comparison: the numerical answer and the IPC-2141/Wadell answer are reported side by side, so the closed form's systematic bias is a measured number in the report rather than a caveat in a docstring.

model_class.description: Pinned. A numerical quasi-static solve is a different class of evidence from exploratory_closed_form and must not be relabelled silently; changing it is a schema revision.

signoff.description: Still false. A 2-D quasi-static solve with nominal laminate data is not controlled-impedance sign-off. What changed versus the closed form is that the error is bounded by refinement instead of unknown - see grid.refinement.grid_error_percent.

signoff_blockers.description: REQUIRED and non-empty: the explicit list of what still stands between this number and sign-off. A tool that cannot say why it is not sign-off will eventually be treated as if it were.

status.description: GREEN: answered, and met --target if one was given. RED: answered but missed the target. NO_COVERAGE: the solve did not converge, or the estimated grid error exceeded --max-grid-error-percent, so the tool refuses to answer rather than reporting a number it cannot stand behind.

inputs.description: Every geometric argument that affected the result, echoed back so the report reproduces without the original command line.

results.description: Single-ended sections report z0_ohm and er_eff; coupled sections report z_diff_ohm, z_odd_ohm, z_even_ohm, z_common_ohm and both modal er_eff values. capacitance_f_per_m is the Maxwell short-circuit matrix in F/m.

closed_form_comparison.description: The IPC-2141/Wadell answer for the SAME geometry, from common.si_models, plus the signed delta. For coax this is instead the exact analytic solution and carries exact:true - that is the geometry the solver is validated against.

notes.description: Includes the rasterisation error. A dimension that had to be snapped to the grid is a real geometry change and is reported rather than absorbed.

refinement.description: Present with --refine. grid_error_percent is a Richardson estimate from two resolutions and is the field a consumer should gate on; the closed form had no equivalent because its bias does not shrink with anything.

verdict.description: The ACCEPTANCE axis, separate from the top-level status. PASS/FAIL only when a criterion was actually applied to a trustworthy value; NO_COVERAGE when none was supplied. The top-level status answers 'did the computation complete', which is why an ungated run can be GREEN there and NO_COVERAGE here. A threshold nobody stated cannot have been met.

verdict_reason.description: Why the acceptance verdict is NO_COVERAGE. Present exactly when no criterion was applied or the value was not trustworthy.

limits.description: Same contract as ipc-calc-report: the honesty notes travel with the machine-readable result, not in a docstring the consumer never sees.
